description: Claude Code finished a long review and ends with 'Want me to make edits 1-4?' — where 1-4 are four numbered items enumerated in full on the screen just above. The regression this guards: the parser emitted question.prompt as that bare line and no tables, so the phone showed two buttons asking the user to approve four edits it never showed them. Everything needed was on screen. A faithful synthetic reproduction of the real pane it was seen on — re-skinned onto tmux-rc's own review loop because the original screen was another codebase's design-doc discussion, which the corpus rules say to scrub. Ends at the agent's 'done' marker, where the question was the live affordance; a later reply would be off-screen.
capture:
▐▛███▛█   Claude Code v2.1.270
▝▜██████▀  Opus 5 · Claude Team
  ▝▝ ▝▝    ~/src/qs/tmux-rc


❯ 195 has review comments what if any minimal changes should I make before standup is copilot happy also?                                                                                                                                                                                    

  Searched for 1 pattern, ran 18 shell commands            

● Where it stands                                            
                                                 
  The human review landed on 9/11 — explicitly "three notes inline, none blocking." The reviewer re-diffed watcher.py against main line by line looking for the dedupe regression that blocked #172, and confirmed there isn't one. So nothing on that side gates merging.

  Copilot is not happy. 14 review passes, last one (9/11 00:19) is 🟡 Changes recommended, with one visible open thread you never replied to plus 3 suppressed findings. Per your own rule about the review loop widening scope past ~3 passes: don't re-request. Pass 14's three
  suppressed items are all parser_prompt.txt scope (the placeholder guard on an empty input box, the "a label is a precedence chain" promise, stale token-cost totals) — that prompt's own business, not this PR's.

  Minimal changes before standup

  1. Resolve the merge conflict — required, 2 minutes. The PR is CONFLICTING/DIRTY now; it wasn't when the review landed. Main moved 20 commits and added the mobile composer row on the line right after the deck ordering in app.js. It's a pure ordering conflict, nothing else
  collides.

  2. Copilot's one open thread (docs/design/architecture.md:219) is correct and cheap. "Pane ids are stable across a restart" genuinely contradicts tmux.py:202, where the watcher rekeys its buffers because a fresh server hands out fresh %N. Narrow the claim to one server
  lifetime and point at the rekey — one clause. This closes Copilot's only cross-cutting finding and is worth doing because the contradiction is inside your own PR.

  3. The note at :109 — the pinned-target env var. It's right that "an accepted UX tradeoff" is quietly carrying a product decision: set TMUXRC_TARGET and the deck is gone from every phone that loads it, and the deck is the entire justification for the daemon running. One
  sentence naming it as accepted product cost. Do this one before standup specifically because it's the kind of thing someone in the room should get to say yes to knowingly.

  4. The note at :104 — event-count semantics. The watcher mints the fingerprint and the classify pass consumes it, so an idle pane stops producing events-log rows, staggered per-pane via cadence. One sentence in Telemetry, plus widen OQ4 from "event inventory" to "events and
  log rows." Cheapest fix is the OQ4 edit alone.

  Bring to standup, don't edit

  The real question isn't in any inline comment — it's the last paragraph of the approval, and it's the only thing that could change the design materially: v1 went from ~250 LOC to ~450 watcher LOC plus two more workstreams, for a defect that is "a card that scrolls out of
  view." It names single-use fingerprint accounting, the versioned capture-format migration, and link rewriting as things that read like they could ship right behind the fix rather than inside it. Go in with a load-bearing-vs-hardening split rather than a doc edit — that's a
  decision to make in the room.

  Skip

  The packaging rewrite (:170). The largest note — split the 447-word v1 scope paragraph into a table/checklist and pull the 352-word protocol spec into a spec block. It's right, and it's mechanical, but it's the biggest edit in the set and the riskiest to do in a rush right
  before standup. Follow-up. (Unless people will be reading the doc in the meeting — then it's the highest-value edit of the five.)

  The carry-forward about nothing building the docs site strictly — already filed as #190.

  Want me to make edits 1–4?                                                                                          
                                                        
✻ Churned for 2m 39s · done 11:39 PM

rows: Resolve the merge conflict in app.js.
Clarify that pane IDs are stable only within one tmux server lifetime; reference rekeying.
Document that TMUXRC_TARGET removes the deck as an accepted product cost.
Clarify event and log-row counting; widen OQ4 to cover both.

expected.headline: Asking whether to make the four minimal edits before the meeting
